## Summary

`terraform plan` cannot run at all against `infra/terraform`. Every terraform operation on this
box is blocked — not just the change that discovered it.

    Error in function call
      on main.tf line 63: user_data = templatefile("${path.module}/user_data.sh", {...})
    Call to function "templatefile" failed: ./user_data.sh:92,24-25: Invalid character;
    This character is not used within the language., and 3 other diagnostic(s).

## Root cause

Merged commit `ef1a7e66a65d` ("Gate standalone shell scripts with ShellCheck") added explanatory
COMMENTS to `infra/terraform/user_data.sh`. Each escapes the FIRST mention of a bash brace
expansion as `$${...}` but leaves the 'reduces to' / 'becomes' half UNESCAPED. Three sites, all
inside `#` comments:

- `:92`  — `# reduces to ${!PARAMS[@]} / ${PARAMS[$name]}. ...`
- `:111` — `# After rendering, "$${!PARAMS[@]}" becomes "${!PARAMS[@]}" ...`

Harmless to bash — a comment is a comment. Fatal to `templatefile()`, which interpolates the
WHOLE file regardless of shell comment syntax and tries to evaluate `${!PARAMS[@]}` as HCL.

## Why this is P1

It blocks ALL terraform work on this box, not one ticket. `-target` does not help: terraform
evaluates the entire configuration before honouring `-target`, so a plan restricted to four SSM
parameters fails identically. There is no narrow path around it.

Discovered while attempting the `terraform apply` that `colourless-hasteless-lamb` needs. That
change (`0f1d0cfc7792`) does NOT touch `user_data.sh` — the file is byte-identical to
`origin/main`, so this is pre-existing and independent.

## Established while diagnosing (useful for whoever fixes it)

- State is REMOTE: S3 `rebar-tfstate-896586841071`, key `rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate`,
  us-east-1, `encrypt = true`, `use_lockfile = true` (no DynamoDB table).
- `terraform init` SUCCEEDS and providers resolve; local CLI 1.15.8 clears the `>= 1.10` floor
  that `use_lockfile` silently requires. So the break is purely the template evaluation.
- When fixed, the change plans as an IN-PLACE update: `user_data_replace_on_change` defaults to
  `false`, so correcting the comments does NOT rebuild the Gerrit box. Worth stating, because
  'terraform wants to change user_data' reads alarming otherwise.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `terraform plan` runs to completion against `infra/terraform`. [non-codebase]
      provenance: environment=fresh worktree /tmp/dd30-wt at origin/main 25ea12c200ae (fix 13e2ea6decc9c62484f80034e28cb96c20448ea2 confirmed an ancestor via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`); principal=arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier (AWS_REGION=us-east-1); privilege_posture=read-only — plan only, `-lock=false`, no apply, no state mutation; instrument=`AWS_REGION=us-east-1 terraform plan -input=false -no-color -lock=false -out=/tmp/dd30.tfplan` returning exit 0 with `Plan: 6 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.` — the outcome is live AWS + S3-remote-state behaviour that no file in the repo can evidence.
- [x] The three comment sites escape BOTH halves (`$$`), or the comments are reworded to avoid
      the sequence entirely. Rewording was chosen. On `origin/main`, an escape-aware scan of
      `infra/terraform/user_data.sh` finds ZERO unescaped `${` that names an undeclared variable.
      The `PARAMS` mentions now read `$${!PARAMS[@]}` / `$${PARAMS[$name]}` (:91) and
      `"$${!PARAMS[@]}"` (:117); the only unescaped interpolations left are the four legitimate
      `${data_volume_id}` sites (:25, :28, :53, :56) plus the `${data_volume_id}` mention at :98,
      which `main.tf:63` actually declares. Verified with `scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py`
      (exit 0), not a naive grep.
- [x] A guard rejects an unescaped `${` in any file consumed by `templatefile()`, so a future
      comment cannot silently break every terraform operation again. ShellCheck cannot catch this
      — the file is valid bash; the breakage is in a different consumer.
      `scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py` exists on `origin/main` and is wired into `make lint`
      (`Makefile:302`). It discovers BOTH `templatefile()` call sites in the tree
      (`infra/terraform/main.tf:63`, `infra/terraform/modules/sso-gate/main.tf:28`) and checks each
      template against that call's own variable map. Confirmed behaviours, read not assumed:
      `EXCLUDED_DIRS` skips `.terraform` (and `.venv`, `node_modules`, the tracker dirs);
      `_DIRECTIVE_KEYWORDS` suppresses `if`/`for`/`in`/`else`/`endif`/`endfor`; `_FOR_BINDINGS`
      admits `%{ for k, v in m }` loop-locals; and `check_repo` tracks those bindings on a `scopes`
      stack across the template so a separate `${k}` later in the loop body resolves. An
      unresolvable call site is reported as `Unresolved` and FAILS rather than passing silently.
      NON-VACUITY PROVED both directions, in a scratch copy, never in the real tree:
      (a) restoring the actual pre-fix file, `git show 13e2ea6decc9c62484f80034e28cb96c20448ea2^:infra/terraform/user_data.sh`,
      makes the guard exit 1 with exactly 3 findings at `user_data.sh:92:14`, `:92:30`, `:111:46` —
      the three sites this bug names, and NOT the escaped `$${!PARAMS[@]}` earlier on line 111,
      so the guard does not miscount escaped as unescaped; (b) removing the seed returns it to
      exit 0; (c) a freshly seeded, line-anchored `echo "seeded mutant ${NOT_A_DECLARED_VAR}"`
      (seed confirmed present by grep before the run) is caught at `:139:21`, exit 1.
      `tests/unit/test_check_templatefile_escapes.py`: 19 passed.
- [x] LIVE VALIDATION — DEFERRED to an operator-supervised deploy window (NOT run in this
      session; not claimed as executed). This bug is the `templatefile()` CODE defect — unescaped
      `${...}` in `user_data.sh` comments — which is FIXED and merged (`13e2ea6decc9`, ancestor of
      origin/main) and re-verified today: real `terraform plan` renders the template cleanly
      (exit 0) and the reported `Invalid character` diagnostic no longer reproduces; the landed
      guard `scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py` is GREEN. The remaining live `terraform apply`
      is out of scope for this code bug and CANNOT be run autonomously — it currently shares one
      physical apply with the `value_wo` secrets migration on `ssm.tf`, which would overwrite prod
      SecureString values with `CHANGEME`. Deferred to the operator-supervised maintenance window
      tracked on `polonium-deceptive-antelope` (f268-32ae-4ea9-42fb) and the value_wo cutover
      `097b-de23-bf12-4c38`. Re-scoped (not `--force`d) so the code fix can close on its own merit.
- [x] Before applying, the plan is REVIEWED and recorded: the three `import` blocks for
      `/rebar/prod/jira-url`, `/rebar/prod/jira-user` and `/rebar/prod/jira-api-token` must ADOPT
      the operator-seeded parameters. If the plan shows any of them DESTROYED, RECREATED, or
      having its value overwritten, STOP — those hold live credentials. REVIEWED: all three are
      ALREADY ADOPTED and the plan proposes NO action on any of them (`no-op` in
      `resource_changes`). The STOP condition does not fire. [non-codebase]
      provenance: environment=fresh worktree /tmp/dd30-wt at origin/main 25ea12c200ae, remote state s3://rebar-tfstate-896586841071/rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate; principal=arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier (AWS_REGION=us-east-1); privilege_posture=read-only — `terraform state list` and `terraform show -json` over a saved plan file, no apply, no state write, and no parameter VALUE printed or logged; instrument=`terraform state list` showing `aws_ssm_parameter.rebar_plain_seeded["/rebar/prod/jira-url"]`, `...["/rebar/prod/jira-user"]` and `aws_ssm_parameter.rebar_secrets["/rebar/prod/jira-api-token"]` at exactly the addresses `infra/terraform/ssm.tf:172-185` imports to, plus `terraform show -json` prior_state recording all three at version=2 with real values (is_CHANGEME=false) — adoption is remote-state and live-AWS fact that no file in the repo can evidence.
- [x] The apply's blast radius is stated: if it proposes changes beyond the four SSM parameters
      and the `user_data` in-place update, that is called out before proceeding. STATED — and it
      DOES exceed that envelope. Full statement in the ticket comment; summary: `6 to add, 1 to
      change, 0 to destroy`, of which TWO adds are beyond the envelope
      (`aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.mcp_mem_abort`, `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.mcp_retire_cap`);
      the `aws_instance.gerrit` in-place `user_data` update STOPS AND STARTS the live Gerrit box
      `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (an outage, not a no-op); and three of the four SSM creates
      (`mcp-client-pat-claude` / `-codex` / `-copilot`) name parameters that ALREADY EXIST in AWS
      at version 1 with NO `import` block, so the apply would fail `ParameterAlreadyExists`
      partway. [non-codebase]
      provenance: environment=fresh worktree /tmp/dd30-wt at origin/main 25ea12c200ae; principal=arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier (AWS_REGION=us-east-1); privilege_posture=read-only — describe/plan-inspection only, no apply and no mutation of AWS or the box; instrument=`terraform show -json /tmp/dd30.tfplan` (per-address actions, `overwrite = null` on all four creates), `aws ssm describe-parameters --parameter-filters Key=Name,Option=BeginsWith,Values=/rebar/prod/mcp-` (metadata only, no values) and `aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids i-00880b2c7f13527c5` — the radius is a property of live AWS state, not of the repo.

## Note

The agent that found this deliberately did NOT edit `user_data.sh` to unblock itself: it is an
unrelated file that feeds production `user_data`, and it belongs in its own reviewed change.
That was the right call.

## Fix plan (added by the agent working this ticket)

### Confirmed mechanism

`templatefile()` interpolates the WHOLE file as an HCL template; `#` is not a comment to it.
`main.tf:63` declares exactly one template variable, `data_volume_id`. An escape-aware scan of
`user_data.sh` (consuming `$$`/`%%` as escapes rather than naive-grepping `${`) finds 7 unescaped
interpolation sequences:

- **4 legitimate** — `:25`, `:28`, `:53`, `:56`, all referencing the declared `data_volume_id`.
  These MUST stay unescaped; they are the feature.
- **3 broken** — `:92:14`, `:92:30`, `:111:46`, all referencing `PARAMS`, a *bash* associative
  array that is not a template variable. Terraform parses `!PARAMS[@]` as HCL and rejects the `!`.

Isolating the template evaluation in a scratch project proved this necessary and sufficient:
escaping only those 3 sites renders the file completely, with all 4 `data_volume_id` sites left
untouched. That is also the reason the guard below must be declared-variable-aware rather than a
blanket ban on `${`.

Origin: `fe4e-54a5-3c3a-4901` (commit `ef1a7e66a65d`), linked `caused_by`. Line 90 predates it and
is correctly escaped, so the carrier walk stops there; the date test confirms regression rather
than an inherited unmet obligation.

### Changes

1. **`infra/terraform/user_data.sh`** — reword the three comment sites so no unescaped `${`
   remains AND the explanation survives. Plain `$$`-escaping of the second half is rejected on
   merit: it makes both halves render identically, so the file that actually lands on the box
   reads "X reduces to X". The comments instead state the escaping RULE and the trap that caused
   this bug, which is strictly more useful than reprinting the post-render form.

2. **`scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py`** (new) — the regression guard. ShellCheck provably
   cannot catch this class: the file is valid bash and the breakage is in a different consumer.
   The guard parses `templatefile(...)` call sites out of the `.tf` files, extracts each call's
   declared variable names, escape-aware-scans the referenced template, and fails on any
   interpolation whose root identifier is not declared. Terraform-native functions (`jsonencode`,
   etc.) are recognised so the existing `config.js.tftpl` stays green.

3. **`Makefile`** — wire into `lint`, following the established `scripts/check_*.py` pattern used
   by the comment-hygiene, raw-git-write and ShellCheck gates.

4. **`tests/unit/test_check_templatefile_escapes.py`** — RED/GREEN/mutation coverage plus the
   `make lint` wiring assertion the sibling gates carry.

### Blast radius

Local. `user_data_replace_on_change` defaults to `false`, so the comment edit plans as an
IN-PLACE `user_data` update and does NOT rebuild the Gerrit instance. No caller depends on the
comment text. The guard is additive and runs static-only.

### Definition of Done

- [x] `terraform plan` completes against `infra/terraform`. Exit 0; see AC1's provenance.
- [x] All 3 broken sites fixed; all 4 legitimate `data_volume_id` sites left intact — confirmed at
      `user_data.sh:25,28,53,56` on `origin/main`, and the guard (which would flag an undeclared
      root) exits 0 with them present, so they were not collaterally escaped.
- [x] Guard observed RED on the broken file, GREEN after the fix, and RED again under a
      re-introduced unescaped sequence (mutation check). All three transitions re-run today
      against `origin/main`; evidence under AC3.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, module-size gate and the touched suites pass — the change
      landed with Gerrit `Verified +1` (CI runs all four), and
      `pytest tests/unit/test_check_templatefile_escapes.py` re-run today: 19 passed.
- [x] `terraform apply` — DEFERRED to the operator-supervised window (NOT run; not claimed as
      executed). Tracked on `polonium-deceptive-antelope` (f268-32ae-4ea9-42fb) / value_wo cutover
      `097b-de23-bf12-4c38`. Out of scope for this templatefile CODE bug; see the LIVE VALIDATION
      note above.
